paragraphs: This page’s checklist supports self-questioning only; it is not a hiring standard, personality assessment, or conclusion about ability. Job authority varies greatly: different organizations assign budget limits, contract signing, personnel decisions, and supplier selection to different roles. No checklist can replace checking the target job’s actual authority.

Use the fictional procurement tasks in A1–A5 to observe yourself: can you specify requirements and acceptance conditions, check two quotes using unit × quantity, and preserve unknowns and escalate to A5’s authorized person after A4 changes delivery timing? The exercise only explores whether you are willing to repeatedly clarify needs, compare supplier conditions, check calculations, and hand over authorization matters over the long term; it is not a suitability score or hiring judgment.

Signals worth considering include willingness to handle interrupted routines, turn vague complaints into observable problems, and accept that your achievements mostly appear as others working smoothly. Signals calling for caution include acting only when needs are fully clear, or an organization making you responsible for costs without corresponding approval and inquiry rights. Clarify the latter boundary before joining.

values: Materials and Assumptions | All Are Editorially Designed Fictional Data

You are the purchasing manager of a fictional organization, evaluating a critical-material purchase and submitting recommendations to authorized people. Suppliers, amounts, dates, specifications, and contract terms are exercise assumptions, not market quotes or organizational policies.

A1 | 2026-09-16 09:00 request: purchase 120 PP-20 filter cartridges with 20-micron filtration, original manufacturer packaging, and no specification substitutions; deliver before 2026-09-23 17:00. Acceptance requires 120 cartridges, undamaged packaging, leak tests passed by 5 sampled cartridges, and batch and conformity certificates; alternative specifications require the engineering lead’s written approval.

A2 | Supplier A quote: CNY 42 per unit × 120 = CNY 5,040; tax included, freight of CNY 240 separately included outside that total and explicitly listed, giving CNY 5,280 overall; delivery 2026-09-22 17:00, 90-day warranty, payment 30 days after acceptance; includes original manufacturer packaging, batch certificates, and transport, excluding on-site installation.

A3 | Supplier B quote: CNY 38 per unit × 120 = CNY 4,560; freight CNY 480, known total CNY 5,040, with tax and packaging costs unspecified; promises delivery on 2026-09-25 17:00, with a 30-day warranty. Availability of 120 cartridges in stock, batch certificates, packaging cost, and liability for delays are unknown; the no-substitution condition is also unconfirmed.

A4 | 2026-09-18 14:00: supplier A reports the originally planned shipment delayed by 2 days, with delivery now expected only on 2026-09-24 17:00; A2’s original delivery condition has changed, directly affecting A1’s deadline on day 23 of month 9. Supplier B remains at day 25 of month 9, without approval to substitute specifications or acceptance conditions.

A5 | Authorization chain: budget ceiling CNY 5,600; the purchasing manager may analyze comparability and make conditional recommendations; the engineering lead approves specification or substitute changes; the finance lead approves over-budget costs and payment conditions; the procurement director signs contracts and orders. If arrival is later than day 23 of month 9, quality certificates are missing, unknown charges may take the total above CNY 5,600, or specifications need changing, escalate within 1 business day and pause ordering.
Tasks and Outputs

Use A1 to establish a needs and acceptance matrix: specifications, quantities, deadlines, quality evidence, and substitution restrictions must be individually checkable. Compare suppliers using A2/A3, distinguishing known totals, unknown costs, delivery times, warranties, responsibilities, and noncomparable conditions.

Use A4 to write a delivery-change escalation request and A5 to document authorization chains for budgets, specification changes, payments, and contract signing; deliver exact calculations, conditional recommendations, clarification questions, authorization requests, and versioned procurement handover records.
Reference Answer (Read After Completing Independently)

Calculation example: A is 42×120 + 240 = CNY 5,280, known to be CNY 320 below CNY 5,600; B is 38×120 + 480 = CNY 5,040 known, but tax and packaging costs are unknown, so CNY 0 cannot be used as the calculated cost. If tax of 13% is used only for a conditional test, 4,560×1.13 + 480 = CNY 5,632.80, still excluding packaging and potentially exceeding budget; this is not a confirmed quote.

After A4, neither supplier directly meets A1’s deadline of 17:00 on day 23 of month 9. A conditional recommendation is first to ask A to confirm in writing within 1 business day the expedited delivery date, batch certificates, and unchanged total of CNY 5,280; if unconfirmed, submit choices of postponement, compliant alternative specifications, or other qualified suppliers to the engineering lead, finance lead, and procurement director, without independently changing specifications, increasing budget, or ordering.

Handover example: record A1–A5 versions, original A and B quotes, known amounts of CNY 5,280 and CNY 5,040, B’s unknown tax, packaging, inventory, and liabilities, A4’s delay notice, proposed reply deadline, and each approver’s pending tasks; until written confirmation is received, mark the status “ordering paused.”
Boundaries and Review

The exercise uses fictional materials only: contact no actual suppliers, make no payments, sign no contracts for others, change no specifications for engineering leads, and approve no budgets for finance leads. B’s tax, packaging, inventory, and delay liabilities remain unknown; unknown costs cannot be treated as zero, and conditional tax-rate calculations must be labeled assumptions. Check correspondence among A1–A5, unit, quantity, and cost calculations, delivery times, quality, contracts, and authorization.
